profile.reading:
Csquare ATL1 sits at 375 Riverside Parkway, Suite 150, Lithia Springs, Georgia 30122, off Interstate 20 in the Atlanta metro. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share, and Csquare's current CEO, Spencer Mullee, previously served as CEO of Evoque before the combined company's formation. Csquare's own spec page states 102,421 square feet of raised floor at ATL1, while the company's SEC Form S-1 property table splits the site into two leased assets, ATL1_A at 56,857 square feet (89.1 percent leased) and ATL1_D at 50,443 square feet (61.5 percent leased), summing to roughly 107,300 square feet, a figure this profile notes as reasonably close to but not identical with the website's single 102,421 square foot total. Csquare states 81.5 megawatts of utility power, 9.2 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 23.5 megawatts of generator capacity for ATL1, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility on its Atlanta page; Georgia Power serves the Atlanta metro as a matter of public record. No reference to Georgia's 2018 House Bill 696 sales-tax exemption expansion was found anywhere in Csquare's own materials for this site, so its applicability to ATL1 is not asserted here. Csquare does not publish a year-opened date for ATL1.

Georgia's data center sector has grown substantially over the past decade, drawing Csquare alongside Switch, QTS, and other operators to the Atlanta metro's I-20 corridor west of downtown, an area offering large developable industrial parcels and proximity to Georgia Power's regional transmission infrastructure. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the filing's only tax-incentive language is a generic risk-factor statement that "certain jurisdictions have provided tax incentives" without naming Georgia or any other specific state.

reading.body:
Centersquare Atlanta ATL1 is a 102,421 square foot raised floor facility in Lithia Springs with 81.5 MW of combined utility power. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this power budget is roughly 2,000 racks. At 8 accelerators per rack, a typical arrangement for large-scale AI workloads, this translates to roughly 16,000 accelerators, though the operator publishes no tenant information or workload specification.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities and only 4 with published power figures, totaling 66.3 MW. This campus ranks fifth among those four published facilities by megawatts, meaning three other Georgia facilities are larger. No certification, security standard, or grid constraint for this facility is published.

Centersquare's parent portfolio is stated by the operator to hold more than 500 MW across 80 facilities in 15 North American markets and London. This single campus represents roughly 16 percent of the operator's stated North American power capacity, making it material to the operator's footprint, but its significance to regional or national AI scaling depends on tenant identity and workload type, which are not published.
